summary: David Pingree was a scholar in Indology and the history of archaeology. Educated at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer, he held posts at Chicago (1963–1971), Brown (from 1971), and Cornell (1981–1986, 1995).

David R. Kinsley worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, learning under Om Prakash Sharma and Virendra Singh, and was on the faculty at McMaster University (1969–2000).

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Carleton, King's College London, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, he taught at NUS (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Ralph Quinter specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at UC Boulder, Stanford (PhD under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure), and the University of Tokyo, later serving as associate professor of East Asian religions at the University of Alberta.
David Reigle works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and was affiliated with the Asian Humanities Press in 2006.

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Cambridge, he held positions at Cambridge colleges, the University of Michigan (1968, 1988–2002), and Harvard University as Pope Professor of Latin (1975–1988).
David Ruddell was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Laval University. He served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford and Harvard University. Joining the University of California, Los Angeles in 1996, he has served there as professor and dean of Humanities (2012).

David Seyfort Ruegg specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at EPHE under Jean Filliozat and Louis Renou, he held chairs and professorships at Leiden University (1966–1972), the University of Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1993–1996).

David Shea was an Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin in 1793 and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College until 1836.
David Slakter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned a master's degree at the University of Liverpool under Christopher Bartley by 2012.
David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar. He completed his studies at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between approximately 1945 and 1952.

David Tracy is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

David W. Chappell worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale, he was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1972–2002) and later taught at Soka University of America (~2002–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, working under teachers including Julia Ching, Robert H. Sharf, and doctoral supervisor James Robson.
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Humboldt University and under Walther Wüst, he held academic posts at Munich (~1947–1951), Alexandria (~1951–1953), and Uppsala University (~1953–1979).
Daw Ohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics. She studied at the University of Rangoon and served there as a Tutor in Pali, attested in 1977.

Dawa Norbu was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Delhi, St. Stephen's, and UC Berkeley. He taught at several institutions in California and served as Professor of Central Asian Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2004).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He held an academic post at Tibet University.
